source_title: MEDKids Small Intestine starter card (demonstration data, unreviewed)
educational_content: The small intestine is a long, twisty tube in the belly. Food moves from the stomach into the small intestine. The small intestine finishes breaking down food. Nutrients from food pass through the walls of the small intestine into the blood. Tiny finger-like bumps called villi help the small intestine take in nutrients. The bloodstream carries the nutrients to the whole body.
learning_objectives: Food moves from the stomach into the small intestine.
Nutrients pass from the small intestine into the blood.
Villi help the small intestine take in nutrients.

forbidden_claims.claim: The small intestine is shorter than the large intestine
Food is digested only in the stomach
